findings.title: FromContext drops contextual log attributes
findings.body: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-asserts infra log's FromContext result to *log.ConcreteLogger and, on failure, returns d.New() with no context. WithContextualAttributes (used by the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware) stores a contextual logger that is not that concrete type, so the assertion fails whenever plugin/request fields were actually attached. LoggerMiddleware then calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), and the completion log is emitted without pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, and uname. The move of contextual logging out of the metrics middleware therefore silently loses those fields in production logs.

findings.title: Plugin completion logs no longer include traceID
findings.body: The previous logRequest path appended traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext whenever a trace was present. That field was removed and is not added by instrumentContext, which only sets endpoint, pluginId, datasource, and user. "Plugin Request Completed" events therefore no longer carry traceID, so request logs cannot be correlated with traces.

findings.title: Nil requests panic before the logger's nil guard
findings.body: QueryData (and CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) dereference req.PluginContext with no nil check. This middleware is registered outside LoggerMiddleware, which explicitly forwards a nil request to next. A nil request now panics in ContextualLoggerMiddleware and never reaches that guard, turning a previously handled case into a crash.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards the logger under test
findings.body: FromContext ignores the receiver and returns NewTestLogger(), a different instance whose Info/Warn/Error calls are not recorded on the TestLogger passed into middleware. Any test that injects TestLogger and asserts on its Logs after LoggerMiddleware calls FromContext(ctx).Info will see zero calls even when a line was logged, so the new logging path cannot be verified with this fake.
